{{short description|Shinto shrine in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|Kumano Hongū Taisha|熊野本宮大社}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shrine Kumano hongu torii01.jpg | caption = Shrine Gate (Torii) of Kumano Hongu Taisha with flag representing [[Yatagarasu]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|50|24|N|135|46|26|E|display=title,inline|source:dewiki}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現) | location = 1110 Hongucho Hongu, [[Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]] 647-1731, Japan }} {{nihongo|'''Kumano Hongū Taisha'''|熊野本宮大社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the jurisdiction of [[Tanabe, Wakayama]], deep in the rugged mountains of the southeast [[Kii Peninsula]] of [[Japan]]. It is included as part of the [[Kumano Sanzan]] in the [[World Heritage Site]] "[[Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range]]". The main deity enshrined is Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現). All of the ancient [[Kumano Kodō]] routes lead to the Grand Shrine. It was originally located at present {{Nihongo|Ōyunohara|大斎原}}, on a sandbank at the [[confluence]] of the [[Kumano River]] and Otonashi River. In 1889, it was partially destroyed in a flood and the remaining shrine buildings were relocated at its present site in 1891. Of the original five main pavilions only three were rebuilt. Four deities were moved there and the other eight are still enshrined there in two stone monuments. [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Torii at Ôyunohara.jpg|alt=Largest Torii in the world|left|thumb|Otorii]] In 2000, the largest [[torii]] shrine gate in the world (33.9 meters tall and 42 meters wide) was erected at the entrance to the Oyunohara sandbank. It is an official gateway that designates the entrance to a sacred area. It signifies the division of the secular and the spiritual worlds. This torii is called ''Otorii'' (''o'' means "great") and is made of steel weighing 172 tons, which took about six months to make and another six months to assemble.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tb-kumano.jp/en/world-heritage/kumano-hongu-taisha/|title = Kumano Hongu Taisha 熊野本宮大社|date = |accessdate = October 9, 2014|website = Sacred Kumano|publisher = Tanabe City Kumona Tourism Bureau|last = |first = }} == History == [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Shaden.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha main temple]] Over 900 years ago a pilgrim wrote of a massive shrine grounds including five main pavilions enshrining 12 deities. Numerous other small temples and shrines could be found surrounding the main buildings. Over the centuries the pavilions were partially destroyed by periodic fires and flooding, but always faithfully rebuilt to their original state. The last fire was in 1776 and the buildings rebuilt again in 1803. The first drawing of the shrine grounds from over 800 years ago and the reconstruction that took place in 1803 are almost exactly identical. After the flood of 1889, the shrine pavilions were moved and rebuilt at their present location. == Architecture == The Kumano Hongu Taisha's pavilions are an outstanding example of Japanese shrine architecture. The use of natural unfinished materials allows it to blend effortlessly into the natural environment. Intricate joint works were used in the construction instead of nails. The thick roof gracefully sweeps forward extending over the stairs and the area in front of the shrine. It is made entirely of hinoki, Japanese cypress bark. [[File:Kumano Hongu Taisha's roof architecture.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha rooftop]] The bronze ornaments on the roof top are characteristic features of shrine architecture. The X-shaped crosspieces that pierce the sky are called Chigi and the log like beams that are laid horizontally along and perpendicular to the ridge line are called Katsuogi. They add a dramatic highlight to the roof line. Unique to the Kumano Hongu Taisha is the space or corridor under the verandas of the pavilions. In the past, the pilgrims and ascetics would use this tiny refuge for meditation, prayer, [[sutra]] copying, austere rites and even sleeping quarters. In fact, this is where Saint [[Ippen|Ippen Shonin]] was enlightened. The Kumano Hongu Taisha is a mixture between Kasuga and Taisha styles but because of this sacred corridor it has also been referred to as the Kumano style. == Festivals == '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Spring Festival''', the annual spring festival held 13–15 April every year, is not only a quintessential festival of Kumano but also intimately associated with the pilgrimage to Kumano and the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. On April 13 fathers and their young sons purify themselves in the [[sacred waters]] of Yunomine Onsen before walking over the Dainichi-goe section of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route to Oyunohara wearing traditional costumes. The young boys have the character for big on their forehead and are forbidden to touch the ground. On April 15 the Kumano Deities are invoked to temporarily take up residence in a portable mikoshi shrine and return to their original site of descend, Oyunohara. The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]
Haiden (Worship Hall) | location = {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Hongu, Tanabe|ja|本宮町本宮}} 1100 | coordinates = {{Coord|33|50|24.9|N|135|46|24.9|E|display=inline,title}} | deities = {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} | shrine_rank = {{ubl|{{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}})|Former {{ill|Kanpei-taisha|ja|官幣大社}}|{{ill|Bekkaku shrine|ja|別表神社}}}} | founded = Traditionally attributed to the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign | pilgrimage = {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} (4th station in Wakayama) | festival = April 15 ([[Kumano Hongu Taisha Grand Festival|御田祭]]) | main_building = {{ubl|{{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (First and Second Halls)|{{ill|Kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} (front) and {{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (rear) (Third and Fourth Halls)}} | map = {{location map|Japan Wakayama|lat_deg=33|lat_min=50|lat_sec=27.1|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=27.4|label=Kumano Hongu Taisha|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|50|27.1|N|135|46|27.4|E}}}} }} '''Kumano Hongu Taisha''' ({{ill|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社}}, ''Kumano Hongū Taisha'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, Japan. Alongside {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|ja|熊野速玉大社}} and {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社}}, it forms the {{ill|Kumano Sanzan|ja|熊野三山}}. The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} as its primary deity and is a key location in the UNESCO World Heritage Site, {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}. == History == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}} at Kumano Hongu Taisha]] The exact date of the shrine's foundation is unknown, but according to legend, it was established in the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign (traditionally 2nd century CE) on a sandbank in the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}}, now known as {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}}. The shrine has been associated with numerous deities and traditions over time. {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}}, often identified with {{ill|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ}}, has unclear origins. Interpretations of the deity vary, ranging from a solar god (due to the association with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, the three-legged crow), a water god (reflecting the shrine's riverside location), to a tree deity. Other theories connect the deity to {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ}}, {{ill|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛}}, or {{ill|Itsukushima|ja|五十猛神}}.{{Cite book|author=川口謙二|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|year=1999|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}} In the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, Kumano Hongu Taisha became a major pilgrimage site, attracting emperors such as {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. By the 12th century, the shrine was one of Japan's most significant religious centers. === Flood and Relocation === In 1889, the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}} flooded, devastating the shrine. Only the {{ill|Kami-sha|ja|上四社}} (First to Fourth Halls) survived and were relocated to the current site. The remaining structures, including the {{ill|Naka-sha|ja|中四社}} and {{ill|Shimo-sha|ja|下四社}}, were not rebuilt. Today, two stone altars at {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}} commemorate the lost shrines. == Deities and Structure == The shrine consists of four main halls, each enshrining different deities: {| class="wikitable" |+ '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Deities and Buddhas''' ! Hall !! name !! deity !! Honji Buddha |- | First Hall || West Front Hall || {{ill|Kumano Musubi Ōkami|ja|熊野牟須美大神}}, {{ill|Kumano Gongen|lt=Koto-sakarai|ja|事解之男神}} || {{ill|Senju Kannon|ja|千手観音}} |- | Second Hall || Central Front Hall || {{ill|Hayatama-no-Mikoto|ja|速玉之男神}} || {{ill|Yakushi Nyorai|ja|薬師如来}} |- | Third Hall || Main Hall || {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} || {{ill|Amida Nyorai|ja|阿弥陀如来}} |- | Fourth Hall || East Front Hall || {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神}} || {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Jūichimen Kannon|ja|十一面観音}} |} The halls, dating to the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, are nationally designated Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web|url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/|title=国指定文化財等データベース|publisher=文化庁}} == Cultural Significance == === Yatagarasu === {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, a three-legged crow, is a symbol of guidance and the shrine's divine messenger. It is believed to have led {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} to the Yamato region, symbolizing wisdom and divine intervention.{{Cite news|title=八咫烏について |publisher=熊野本宮大社|url=http://www.hongutaisha.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%92%AB%E7%83%8F/|accessdate=2020-03-23}} === UNESCO World Heritage === Kumano Hongu Taisha is part of the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004. == Access == * '''Bus:''' From {{ill|JR Shingu Station|ja|新宮駅}}, 1 hour via Kumano Kotsu buses. * {{short description|Shinto shrine in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|Kumano Hongū Taisha|熊野本宮大社}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shrine Kumano hongu torii01.jpg | caption = Shrine Gate (Torii) of Kumano Hongu Taisha with flag representing [[Yatagarasu]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|50|24|N|135|46|26|E|display=title,inline|source:dewiki}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現) | location = 1110 Hongucho Hongu, [[Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]] 647-1731, Japan }} {{nihongo|'''Kumano Hongū Taisha'''|熊野本宮大社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the jurisdiction of [[Tanabe, Wakayama]], deep in the rugged mountains of the southeast [[Kii Peninsula]] of [[Japan]]. It is included as part of the [[Kumano Sanzan]] in the [[World Heritage Site]] "[[Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range]]". The main deity enshrined is Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現). All of the ancient [[Kumano Kodō]] routes lead to the Grand Shrine. It was originally located at present {{Nihongo|Ōyunohara|大斎原}}, on a sandbank at the [[confluence]] of the [[Kumano River]] and Otonashi River. In 1889, it was partially destroyed in a flood and the remaining shrine buildings were relocated at its present site in 1891. Of the original five main pavilions only three were rebuilt. Four deities were moved there and the other eight are still enshrined there in two stone monuments. [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Torii at Ôyunohara.jpg|alt=Largest Torii in the world|left|thumb|Otorii]] In 2000, the largest [[torii]] shrine gate in the world (33.9 meters tall and 42 meters wide) was erected at the entrance to the Oyunohara sandbank. It is an official gateway that designates the entrance to a sacred area. It signifies the division of the secular and the spiritual worlds. This torii is called ''Otorii'' (''o'' means "great") and is made of steel weighing 172 tons, which took about six months to make and another six months to assemble.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tb-kumano.jp/en/world-heritage/kumano-hongu-taisha/|title = Kumano Hongu Taisha 熊野本宮大社|date = |accessdate = October 9, 2014|website = Sacred Kumano|publisher = Tanabe City Kumona Tourism Bureau|last = |first = }} == History == [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Shaden.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha main temple]] Over 900 years ago a pilgrim wrote of a massive shrine grounds including five main pavilions enshrining 12 deities. Numerous other small temples and shrines could be found surrounding the main buildings. Over the centuries the pavilions were partially destroyed by periodic fires and flooding, but always faithfully rebuilt to their original state. The last fire was in 1776 and the buildings rebuilt again in 1803. The first drawing of the shrine grounds from over 800 years ago and the reconstruction that took place in 1803 are almost exactly identical. After the flood of 1889, the shrine pavilions were moved and rebuilt at their present location. == Architecture == The Kumano Hongu Taisha's pavilions are an outstanding example of Japanese shrine architecture. The use of natural unfinished materials allows it to blend effortlessly into the natural environment. Intricate joint works were used in the construction instead of nails. The thick roof gracefully sweeps forward extending over the stairs and the area in front of the shrine. It is made entirely of hinoki, Japanese cypress bark. [[File:Kumano Hongu Taisha's roof architecture.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha rooftop]] The bronze ornaments on the roof top are characteristic features of shrine architecture. The X-shaped crosspieces that pierce the sky are called Chigi and the log like beams that are laid horizontally along and perpendicular to the ridge line are called Katsuogi. They add a dramatic highlight to the roof line. Unique to the Kumano Hongu Taisha is the space or corridor under the verandas of the pavilions. In the past, the pilgrims and ascetics would use this tiny refuge for meditation, prayer, [[sutra]] copying, austere rites and even sleeping quarters. In fact, this is where Saint [[Ippen|Ippen Shonin]] was enlightened. The Kumano Hongu Taisha is a mixture between Kasuga and Taisha styles but because of this sacred corridor it has also been referred to as the Kumano style. == Festivals == '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Spring Festival''', the annual spring festival held 13–15 April every year, is not only a quintessential festival of Kumano but also intimately associated with the pilgrimage to Kumano and the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. On April 13 fathers and their young sons purify themselves in the [[sacred waters]] of Yunomine Onsen before walking over the Dainichi-goe section of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route to Oyunohara wearing traditional costumes. The young boys have the character for big on their forehead and are forbidden to touch the ground. On April 15 the Kumano Deities are invoked to temporarily take up residence in a portable mikoshi shrine and return to their original site of descend, Oyunohara. The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]

The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]
Haiden (Worship Hall) | location = {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Hongu, Tanabe|ja|本宮町本宮}} 1100 | coordinates = {{Coord|33|50|24.9|N|135|46|24.9|E|display=inline,title}} | deities = {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} | shrine_rank = {{ubl|{{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社}})|Former {{ill|Kanpei-taisha|ja|官幣大社}}|{{ill|Bekkaku shrine|ja|別表神社}}}} | founded = Traditionally attributed to the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign | pilgrimage = {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} (4th station in Wakayama) | festival = April 15 ([[Kumano Hongu Taisha Grand Festival|御田祭]]) | main_building = {{ubl|{{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (First and Second Halls)|{{ill|Kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} (front) and {{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (rear) (Third and Fourth Halls)}} | map = {{location map|Japan Wakayama|lat_deg=33|lat_min=50|lat_sec=27.1|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=27.4|label=Kumano Hongu Taisha|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|50|27.1|N|135|46|27.4|E}}}} }} '''Kumano Hongu Taisha''' ({{ill|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社}}, ''Kumano Hongū Taisha'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, Japan. Alongside {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|ja|熊野速玉大社}} and {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社}}, it forms the {{ill|Kumano Sanzan|ja|熊野三山}}. The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} as its primary deity and is a key location in the UNESCO World Heritage Site, {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}. == History == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}} at Kumano Hongu Taisha]] The exact date of the shrine's foundation is unknown, but according to legend, it was established in the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign (traditionally 2nd century CE) on a sandbank in the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}}, now known as {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}}. The shrine has been associated with numerous deities and traditions over time. {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}}, often identified with {{ill|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ}}, has unclear origins. Interpretations of the deity vary, ranging from a solar god (due to the association with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, the three-legged crow), a water god (reflecting the shrine's riverside location), to a tree deity. Other theories connect the deity to {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ}}, {{ill|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛}}, or {{ill|Itsukushima|ja|五十猛神}}.{{Cite book|author=川口謙二|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|year=1999|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}} In the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, Kumano Hongu Taisha became a major pilgrimage site, attracting emperors such as {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. By the 12th century, the shrine was one of Japan's most significant religious centers. === Flood and Relocation === In 1889, the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}} flooded, devastating the shrine. Only the {{ill|Kami-sha|ja|上四社}} (First to Fourth Halls) survived and were relocated to the current site. The remaining structures, including the {{ill|Naka-sha|ja|中四社}} and {{ill|Shimo-sha|ja|下四社}}, were not rebuilt. Today, two stone altars at {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}} commemorate the lost shrines. == Deities and Structure == The shrine consists of four main halls, each enshrining different deities: {| class="wikitable" |+ '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Deities and Buddhas''' ! Hall !! name !! deity !! Honji Buddha |- | First Hall || West Front Hall || {{ill|Kumano Musubi Ōkami|ja|熊野牟須美大神}}, {{ill|Kumano Gongen|lt=Koto-sakarai|ja|事解之男神}} || {{ill|Senju Kannon|ja|千手観音}} |- | Second Hall || Central Front Hall || {{ill|Hayatama-no-Mikoto|ja|速玉之男神}} || {{ill|Yakushi Nyorai|ja|薬師如来}} |- | Third Hall || Main Hall || {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} || {{ill|Amida Nyorai|ja|阿弥陀如来}} |- | Fourth Hall || East Front Hall || {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神}} || {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Jūichimen Kannon|ja|十一面観音}} |} The halls, dating to the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, are nationally designated Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web|url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/|title=国指定文化財等データベース|publisher=文化庁}} == Cultural Significance == === Yatagarasu === {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, a three-legged crow, is a symbol of guidance and the shrine's divine messenger. It is believed to have led {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} to the Yamato region, symbolizing wisdom and divine intervention.{{Cite news|title=八咫烏について |publisher=熊野本宮大社|url=http://www.hongutaisha.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%92%AB%E7%83%8F/|accessdate=2020-03-23}} === UNESCO World Heritage === Kumano Hongu Taisha is part of the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004. == Access == * '''Bus:''' From {{ill|JR Shingu Station|ja|新宮駅}}, 1 hour via Kumano Kotsu buses. * '''Car:''' Parking available. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.hongutaisha.jp/ Official Website of Kumano Hongu Taisha] * revision.text:
{{神社 |名称 = 熊野本宮大社 |画像 = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = 〒647-1731 [[和歌山県]][[田辺市]][[本宮町本宮]]1100 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|33|50|24.9|N|135|46|24.9|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[熊野権現|家都美御子大神]] |社格 = [[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）
旧[[官幣大社]]
[[別表神社]] |創建 = 伝・[[崇神天皇]]65年 |札所等 = [[神仏霊場巡拝の道]]第4番（和歌山第4番） |例祭 = 4月15日（[[熊野本宮大社例大祭|御田祭]]） |本殿 = [[入母屋造]]（第一殿・第二殿）、[[切妻造]]（正面）・[[入母屋造]]（背面）（第三殿・第四殿） |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Wakayama|lat_deg=33|lat_min=50|lat_sec=27.1|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=27.4|label=熊野
本宮大社|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|50|27.1|N|135|46|27.4|E}}}} }} '''熊野本宮大社'''（くまのほんぐうたいしゃ）は、[[和歌山県]][[田辺市]][[本宮町本宮]]にある[[神社]]。[[熊野速玉大社]]・[[熊野那智大社]]と共に、[[熊野三山]]を構成している。[[熊野権現|家都美御子大神]]（けつみみこのおおかみ、熊野坐大神〈くまぬにますおおかみ〉、熊野加武呂乃命〈くまぬかむろのみこと〉とも）を主祭神とする。かつては[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[官幣大社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。[[国際連合教育科学文化機関|ユネスコ]]の[[世界遺産]]「[[紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道]]」の構成資産の1つ。 == 歴史 == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|熊野本宮大社 [[八咫烏]]の像]] 詳しい創建年代は不明であるが、社伝によると[[崇神天皇]]65年に[[熊野川]]の中洲、現在の大斎原（おおゆのはら）の地に創建されたとされている。 「[[長寛勘文|熊野権現垂迹縁起]]」によると、熊野坐大神は[[唐]]の[[天台山]]から飛来したとされている。熊野坐大神（家都美御子大神）は、[[スサノオ|須佐之男命]]とされるが、その素性は不明である。太陽の使いとされる[[八咫烏]]を神使とすることから太陽神であるという説や、中洲に鎮座していたことから水神とする説、または木の神とする説などがある。家都美御子大神については他にも[[五十猛神]]や[[伊邪那美神]]とする説があり、[[菊理媛神]]とも関係するとの説もあるが、やはりその素性は不詳とされる{{Cite book|和書|author=川口 謙二（編著）|year=1999|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}}。 古代から中世にかけて、神職は[[ニギハヤヒ]]の後裔で[[熊野国造]]の流れを汲む[[和田氏]]が世襲し、[[平安時代]]には[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）に列せられている。 [[平安時代]]の末期には[[鳥羽天皇|鳥羽上皇]]、[[後白河天皇|後白河法皇]]、[[後鳥羽天皇|後鳥羽上皇]]などが幾度も[[熊野三山]]に足を運び、大いに賑わっている。 [[1871年]]（[[明治]]4年）に'''熊野座神社'''（くまのにますじんじゃ）として[[国幣中社]]に列格した。 かつては熊野川の中洲に上四社、中四社、下四社を始め拝殿や様々な社殿が立ち並んでいたが、 [[1889年]]（明治22年）8月に[[十津川大水害]]が発生。和歌山県田辺で日雨量901.7mmを観測する記録的な豪雨に加え、上流の奈良県側に降った豪雨の影響もあり熊野川は大洪水となった。それまでは社殿が流される規模の出水は無かったが、このときの雨で{{Cite book |和書 |author=北原糸子 編、松浦律子 編、木村玲欧 編 |title=日本歴史災害事典 |publisher=吉川弘文社 |date=2012-06-11 |page=356 |isbn=9784642014687 }}上四社以外の建物は全て流されてしまった。明治以後、山林の伐採が急激に行われたことにより山林の保水力が失われ、大規模な洪水が引き起こされたもようである。残された上四社は現在地に移転したが、中四社、下四社と様々な摂末社の再建は行われなかった。旧社地の中洲は大斎原（おおゆのはら）と呼ばれ、中四社、下四社と摂末社の祭神を祀る2基の石祠が建立されたなお、その時の大洪水で被災した上流の[[十津川村]]集落の住民の一部が移住した先で開墾したのが[[北海道]]の[[新十津川村]]である。。 [[1915年]]（[[大正]]4年）には[[官幣大社]]に昇格している。[[1948年]]（[[昭和]]23年）に[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に加列されている。 [[2000年]]（[[平成]]12年）、大斎原に[[鉄筋コンクリート造]]の日本一高い大鳥居（高さ33.9m、横42m）が建てられた。 かつては[[湯立]]が行われており、「熊野権現垂迹縁起」では大斎原が「大湯原」と表記されていることや、熊野をユヤと読む際に湯屋や湯谷の字をあてられたことなどから、熊野信仰の中核に湯の観念があったことが指摘されている{{Cite book|和書|author=鈴木正崇|year=2008|title=宗教民俗研究|chapter=熊野信仰と湯立神楽|volume=18|page=28|issn=0917-9143}}[[鈴木正崇]]『熊野と[[神楽]]―[[聖地]]の根源的力を求めて』[[平凡社]]、2018年、13頁。ISBN 978-4-582-36452-1。 === 八咫烏 === 日本を統一した[[神武天皇]]を[[大和国]]の橿原（現・[[橿原市]]）まで先導したという[[神武東征]]の故事に習い、導きの神として[[八咫烏]]には篤い信仰がある{{r|烏}}。[[八咫烏]]の「八咫」とは大きく広いという意味である{{r|烏}}。太陽の化身で三本の足があり、それぞれ天・地・人をあらわす、といわれている{{Cite news|title=八咫烏について |publisher=熊野本宮大社|url=http://www.hongutaisha.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%92%AB%E7%83%8F/|accessdate=2020-03-23}}。 JFA（[[日本サッカー協会]]）のマークも八咫烏である{{r|烏}}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://gendai.media/articles/-/79996?imp=0|title=3本足のカラス「ヤタガラス」の伝説とは…蹴鞠とサッカーの奥深い関係|publisher=講談社|author=秋尾沙戸子　東村アキコ|date=2021-02-07|accessdate=2021-07-31}}。多くの[[サッカー]]関係者が必勝祈願に訪れている{{r|烏}}。 ちなみに、サッカーを初めて日本に紹介した[[中村覚之助 (サッカー指導者)|中村覚之助]]（[[1878年]] - [[1906年]]）は那智町（現・[[那智勝浦町]]）の出身{{r|講談社}}。[[西日本旅客鉄道|JR西日本]][[那智駅]]前には「日本サッカーの始祖 中村覚之助」と刻まれた顕彰碑がある{{Cite news|title=サッカーＷ杯、“聖地”で日本代表の応援を－「八咫烏」など縁が深い和歌山県がキャンペーン |publisher=[[産経新聞|産経]]ＷＥＳＴ|url=https://www.sankei.com/article/20171227-KHLE4B2Z4ZPMRKAUIUOAUGWGN4/|date=2017-12-27|accessdate=2020-03-23}}。 == 祭神 == {|class="wikitable" style="width:100%;" |+'''表 熊野本宮大社の社殿・祭神・[[本地垂迹説|本地仏]]''' |- !colspan="3"|社殿 !祭神 !本地仏 |- !rowspan="4"|上四社 !第一殿 !西御前 |熊野牟須美大神・事解之男神 |[[千手観音]] |- !第二殿 !中御前 |速玉之男神 |[[薬師如来]] |- !第三殿 !證証殿 |'''家都美御子大神''' |[[阿弥陀如来]] |- !第四殿 !若宮 |[[アマテラス|天照大神]] |[[十一面観音]] |- !rowspan="4"|中四社 !第五殿 !禅児宮 |[[アメノオシホミミ|忍穂耳命]] |[[地蔵菩薩]] |- !第六殿 !聖宮 |[[ニニギ|瓊々杵尊]] |[[龍樹|龍樹菩薩]] |- !第七殿 !児宮 |[[ホオリ|彦火火出見尊]] |[[如意輪観音]] |- !第八殿 !子守宮 |[[ウガヤフキアエズ|鵜葺草葺不合命]] |[[聖観音]] |- !rowspan="4"|下四社 !第九殿 !一万十万 |[[カグツチ|軻遇突智命]] |[[文殊菩薩]]・[[普賢菩薩]] |- !第十殿 !米持金剛 |[[ハニヤス|埴山姫命]] |[[毘沙門天]] |- !第十一殿 !飛行夜叉 |[[ミヅハノメ|弥都波能売命]] |[[不動明王]] |- !第十二殿 !勧請十五所 |[[ワクムスビ|稚産霊命]] |[[釈迦如来]] |} 前述の通り、1889年（明治22年）の熊野川水害により中洲にあった社殿は大きな被害を受け、上四社のみが現社地に移築された。中四社および下四社と摂末社の社殿は再建されず、旧社地に2基の石祠が建てられた[https://www.hongu.jp/kumanokodo/hongu-taisya/ooyunohara/ 熊野本宮大社旧社地「大斎原」]。なお神域内の上四社・大斎原とも基本的に撮影禁止であり、撮影を希望する場合は社務所にて許可が必要である。 == 境内 == * 本宮（第三殿（證証殿）、[[重要文化財]]） - 祭神：家都美御子大神。[[文化 (元号)|文化]]7年（[[1810年]]）建立。 * 結宮（第一殿（西御前）・第二殿（中御前）、重要文化財） - 第一殿祭神：熊野牟須美大神・事解之男神、第二殿祭神：速玉之男神。[[享和]]2年（[[1802年]]）建立。 * 若宮（第四殿（東御前）、重要文化財） - 祭神：[[アマテラス|天照大神]]。享和2年（1802年）建立。 * 中門 - 4つ並んでいる。 * 満山社 - 祭神：結びの神、祓いの神 * 拝殿 * 神門 * [[八咫烏]]像 * 社務所 * 宝物殿 * [[祓戸大神]] * 功霊社 - 祭神：[[日露戦争]]と[[太平洋戦争]]での戦死者 * 瑞鳳殿 * 境外 ** 産田社 - 祭神：[[イザナミ|伊邪那美大神]][[荒魂]] === 熊野本宮旧社地 大斎原 === * 大鳥居 - [[鉄筋コンクリート造]]の日本一高い大鳥居。高さ33.9m、横42m。[[2000年]]（[[平成]]12年）完成。 * 東の石祠 - 祭神：境内摂末社（八咫烏神社・音無天神社・高倉下神社・海神社） * 西の石祠 - 祭神：中四社（[[アメノオシホミミ|忍穂耳命]]・[[ニニギ|瓊々杵尊]]・[[ホオリ|彦火火出見尊]]・[[ウガヤフキアエズ|鵜葺草葺不合命]]）、下四社（[[カグツチ|軻遇突智命]]・[[ハニヤス|埴山姫命]]・[[ミヅハノメ|弥都波能売命]]・[[ワクムスビ|稚産霊命]]） Kumano Kodo Kumano Hongu Taisha World heritage 文化財 == [[ファイル:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Yatagarasu-Postbox.jpg|thumb|200px|right|八咫烏ポスト]] === 重要文化財 === ==== 建造物 ==== * 熊野本宮大社 - 重要文化財（建造物、[[1995年]]（[[平成]]7年）12月26日指定）{{Cite web|和書 |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/ |title=国指定文化財等データベース |publisher=文化庁 |accessdate=2010-06-12 }} ** 熊野本宮大社第一殿・第二殿（西御前・中御前）{{国指定文化財等データベース2 |name=熊野本宮大社 第一殿・第二殿（西御前・中御前） |register=102 |item=2926 |accessdate=2010-06-12}} ** 熊野本宮大社第三殿（証誠殿）{{国指定文化財等データベース2 |name=熊野本宮大社 第三殿（証誠殿） |register=102 |item=2927 |accessdate=2010-06-12}} ** 熊野本宮大社第四殿（若一王子）{{国指定文化財等データベース2 |name=熊野本宮大社 第四殿（若一王子） |register=102 |item=2928 |accessdate=2010-06-12}} 上記3棟が[[重要文化財]]に指定されている（第一・二殿は建物としては1棟）。棟札により、第一・二殿と第四殿は[[享和]]2年（[[1802年]]）、第三殿は[[文化 (元号)|文化]]7年（[[1810年]]）の建立と判明する。第一・二殿は入母屋造平入り、桁行5間、梁間4間で、正面に庇を付し、正面の2箇所に木階を設ける。内部は桁行3間、梁間1間の内陣とし、3室に分け、左右の室に熊野牟須美大神と速玉之男神をそれぞれ祀る。第一・二殿の向かって右に建つ第三殿と第四殿は同規模・同形式で妻入り、正面は切妻造庇付き、背面は入母屋造の特異な形式とする。柱間は桁行（本建物の場合は側面）2間、梁間は正面は1間、背面は中央に柱が立ち2間とする。これらの社殿は[[1889年]]（[[明治]]22年）の[[十津川大水害]]での流出を免れ、現社地に移築されたものである。各建物は入母屋造屋根を用いる点、木割が太く、装飾の少ない簡素な構成とする点に特色があり、床下に[[連子窓]]を設けるなど、細部形式にも特色がある。社殿の形式や配置は中世の絵画資料にみられるものと一致し、古くからの形式を保持していることがわかる本段落の解説は次の文献による。『月刊文化財』388号、第一法規、1986年1月、pp.9 - 13。 ==== 美術工芸品 ==== * 木造家津御子大神坐像、木造速玉大神坐像 、木造夫須美大神坐像、附 木造天照大神坐像（1966年〈昭和41年〉6月11日・4躯一括指定）。 * 鉄湯釜（[[1983年]]（[[昭和]]58年）6月6日指定）{{国指定文化財等データベース2 |name=鉄湯釜 |register=201 |item=7243 |year=1983 |jyear=昭和58 |month=6 |date=6 |cat1=重要文化財 |cat2= |class=美術工芸品 |accessdate=2010-06-12 }} - 湯立ての神事に用いる湯釜で、[[建久]]9年（[[1198年]]）の銘がある。鉄製の湯船としては建久8年（[[1197年]]）在銘の[[東大寺]]大湯屋のものが最古であるが、湯釜としては本品が在銘最古の遺品である『月刊文化財』237号、第一法規、1983年6月、pp.13 - 14。 === 国指定史跡 === * [[熊野三山]] - 熊野本宮大社境内は史跡「熊野三山」の一部である{{国指定文化財等データベース2 |name=熊野三山 |register=401 |item=3364 |year=2000 |jyear=平成12 |month=11 |date=2 |year2=2002 |jyear2=平成14 |month2=12 |date2=19 |additional=分離・追加指定・名称変更 |cat1=史跡 |accessdate=2010-06-12 }}。当初、本宮大社社地は大斎原（本宮大社旧社地）のみが史跡「[[熊野古道|熊野参詣道]]」の一部として史跡として指定を受けていたが、[[2002年]]（平成14年）12月19日、熊野三山が熊野参詣道から分離・名称変更された際に、現社地が追加指定された{{Cite web|和書 |author=文部科学省 |authorlink=文部科学省 |date=2002-11-15 |url=http://www.mext.go.jp/b_menu/shingi/bunka/toushin/021204.htm |title=史跡等の指定等について |accessdate=2010-06-13 }}。 === 和歌山県指定有形文化財 === * 絹本著色熊野本宮八葉曼荼羅 1幅 - [[南北朝時代 (日本)|南北朝時代]]後期から[[室町時代]]。 * [[熊野本宮大社例大祭#大日越え|大日堂の石仏]] 1躯 * 熊野本宮大社奉納鏡 16面 * 儀仗鉾 2振 * 擬宝珠 3個 - 江戸時代初期。[[元和 (日本)|元和]]6年（[[1620年]]）。[[紀州藩]]主[[徳川頼宣]]奉納。 * 若狭国主酒井忠直奉納石硯 1面 * 神額 1面 - 江戸時代初期。[[慶長]]18年（[[1613年]]）。豊臣秀頼寄進。 * 銅鍍金つり灯呂 1対 - 豊臣秀頼寄進。 * 銅鉢 1口 - 豊臣秀頼寄進。 * 文台 1基 * 硯箱 1基 === 和歌山県指定無形民俗文化財 === * 八咫烏神事（熊野本宮大社神事保存会） * 御竈木神事（熊野本宮大社神事保存会） * 熊野本宮の湯登神事・御田祭（熊野本宮大社神事保存会） == 前後の札所 == ; {{short description|Shinto shrine in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|Kumano Hongū Taisha|熊野本宮大社}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shrine Kumano hongu torii01.jpg | caption = Shrine Gate (Torii) of Kumano Hongu Taisha with flag representing [[Yatagarasu]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|50|24|N|135|46|26|E|display=title,inline|source:dewiki}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現) | location = 1110 Hongucho Hongu, [[Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]] 647-1731, Japan }} {{nihongo|'''Kumano Hongū Taisha'''|熊野本宮大社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the jurisdiction of [[Tanabe, Wakayama]], deep in the rugged mountains of the southeast [[Kii Peninsula]] of [[Japan]]. It is included as part of the [[Kumano Sanzan]] in the [[World Heritage Site]] "[[Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range]]". The main deity enshrined is Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現). All of the ancient [[Kumano Kodō]] routes lead to the Grand Shrine. It was originally located at present {{Nihongo|Ōyunohara|大斎原}}, on a sandbank at the [[confluence]] of the [[Kumano River]] and Otonashi River. In 1889, it was partially destroyed in a flood and the remaining shrine buildings were relocated at its present site in 1891. Of the original five main pavilions only three were rebuilt. Four deities were moved there and the other eight are still enshrined there in two stone monuments. [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Torii at Ôyunohara.jpg|alt=Largest Torii in the world|left|thumb|Otorii]] In 2000, the largest [[torii]] shrine gate in the world (33.9 meters tall and 42 meters wide) was erected at the entrance to the Oyunohara sandbank. It is an official gateway that designates the entrance to a sacred area. It signifies the division of the secular and the spiritual worlds. This torii is called ''Otorii'' (''o'' means "great") and is made of steel weighing 172 tons, which took about six months to make and another six months to assemble.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tb-kumano.jp/en/world-heritage/kumano-hongu-taisha/|title = Kumano Hongu Taisha 熊野本宮大社|date = |accessdate = October 9, 2014|website = Sacred Kumano|publisher = Tanabe City Kumona Tourism Bureau|last = |first = }} == History == [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Shaden.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha main temple]] Over 900 years ago a pilgrim wrote of a massive shrine grounds including five main pavilions enshrining 12 deities. Numerous other small temples and shrines could be found surrounding the main buildings. Over the centuries the pavilions were partially destroyed by periodic fires and flooding, but always faithfully rebuilt to their original state. The last fire was in 1776 and the buildings rebuilt again in 1803. The first drawing of the shrine grounds from over 800 years ago and the reconstruction that took place in 1803 are almost exactly identical. After the flood of 1889, the shrine pavilions were moved and rebuilt at their present location. == Architecture == The Kumano Hongu Taisha's pavilions are an outstanding example of Japanese shrine architecture. The use of natural unfinished materials allows it to blend effortlessly into the natural environment. Intricate joint works were used in the construction instead of nails. The thick roof gracefully sweeps forward extending over the stairs and the area in front of the shrine. It is made entirely of hinoki, Japanese cypress bark. [[File:Kumano Hongu Taisha's roof architecture.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha rooftop]] The bronze ornaments on the roof top are characteristic features of shrine architecture. The X-shaped crosspieces that pierce the sky are called Chigi and the log like beams that are laid horizontally along and perpendicular to the ridge line are called Katsuogi. They add a dramatic highlight to the roof line. Unique to the Kumano Hongu Taisha is the space or corridor under the verandas of the pavilions. In the past, the pilgrims and ascetics would use this tiny refuge for meditation, prayer, [[sutra]] copying, austere rites and even sleeping quarters. In fact, this is where Saint [[Ippen|Ippen Shonin]] was enlightened. The Kumano Hongu Taisha is a mixture between Kasuga and Taisha styles but because of this sacred corridor it has also been referred to as the Kumano style. == Festivals == '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Spring Festival''', the annual spring festival held 13–15 April every year, is not only a quintessential festival of Kumano but also intimately associated with the pilgrimage to Kumano and the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. On April 13 fathers and their young sons purify themselves in the [[sacred waters]] of Yunomine Onsen before walking over the Dainichi-goe section of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route to Oyunohara wearing traditional costumes. The young boys have the character for big on their forehead and are forbidden to touch the ground. On April 15 the Kumano Deities are invoked to temporarily take up residence in a portable mikoshi shrine and return to their original site of descend, Oyunohara. The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]
Haiden (Worship Hall) | location = {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Hongu, Tanabe|ja|本宮町本宮}} 1100 | coordinates = {{Coord|33|50|24.9|N|135|46|24.9|E|display=inline,title}} | deities = {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} | shrine_rank = {{ubl|{{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}})|Former {{ill|Kanpei-taisha|ja|官幣大社}}|{{ill|Bekkaku shrine|ja|別表神社}}}} | founded = Traditionally attributed to the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign | pilgrimage = {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} (4th station in Wakayama) | festival = April 15 ([[Kumano Hongu Taisha Grand Festival|御田祭]]) | main_building = {{ubl|{{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (First and Second Halls)|{{ill|Kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} (front) and {{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (rear) (Third and Fourth Halls)}} | map = {{location map|Japan Wakayama|lat_deg=33|lat_min=50|lat_sec=27.1|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=27.4|label=Kumano Hongu Taisha|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|50|27.1|N|135|46|27.4|E}}}} }} '''Kumano Hongu Taisha''' ({{ill|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社}}, ''Kumano Hongū Taisha'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, Japan. Alongside {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|ja|熊野速玉大社}} and {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社}}, it forms the {{ill|Kumano Sanzan|ja|熊野三山}}. The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} as its primary deity and is a key location in the UNESCO World Heritage Site, {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}. == History == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}} at Kumano Hongu Taisha]] The exact date of the shrine's foundation is unknown, but according to legend, it was established in the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign (traditionally 2nd century CE) on a sandbank in the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}}, now known as {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}}. The shrine has been associated with numerous deities and traditions over time. {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}}, often identified with {{ill|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ}}, has unclear origins. Interpretations of the deity vary, ranging from a solar god (due to the association with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, the three-legged crow), a water god (reflecting the shrine's riverside location), to a tree deity. Other theories connect the deity to {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ}}, {{ill|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛}}, or {{ill|Itsukushima|ja|五十猛神}}.{{Cite book|author=川口謙二|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|year=1999|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}} In the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, Kumano Hongu Taisha became a major pilgrimage site, attracting emperors such as {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|後白河天皇}}. By the 12th century, the shrine was one of Japan's most significant religious centers. === Flood and Relocation === In 1889, the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}} flooded, devastating the shrine. Only the {{ill|Kami-sha|ja|上四社}} (First to Fourth Halls) survived and were relocated to the current site. The remaining structures, including the {{ill|Naka-sha|ja|中四社}} and {{ill|Shimo-sha|ja|下四社}}, were not rebuilt. Today, two stone altars at {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}} commemorate the lost shrines. == Deities and Structure == The shrine consists of four main halls, each enshrining different deities: {| class="wikitable" |+ '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Deities and Buddhas''' ! Hall !! name !! deity !! Honji Buddha |- | First Hall || West Front Hall || {{ill|Kumano Musubi Ōkami|ja|熊野牟須美大神}}, {{ill|Kumano Gongen|lt=Koto-sakarai|ja|事解之男神}} || {{ill|Senju Kannon|ja|千手観音}} |- | Second Hall || Central Front Hall || {{ill|Hayatama-no-Mikoto|ja|速玉之男神}} || {{ill|Yakushi Nyorai|ja|薬師如来}} |- | Third Hall || Main Hall || {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} || {{ill|Amida Nyorai|ja|阿弥陀如来}} |- | Fourth Hall || East Front Hall || {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神}} || {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Jūichimen Kannon|ja|十一面観音}} |} The halls, dating to the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, are nationally designated Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web|url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/|title=国指定文化財等データベース|publisher=文化庁}} == Cultural Significance == === Yatagarasu === {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, a three-legged crow, is a symbol of guidance and the shrine's divine messenger. It is believed to have led {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} to the Yamato region, symbolizing wisdom and divine intervention.{{Cite news|title=八咫烏について |publisher=熊野本宮大社|url=http://www.hongutaisha.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%92%AB%E7%83%8F/|accessdate=2020-03-23}} === UNESCO World Heritage === Kumano Hongu Taisha is part of the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004. == Access == * '''Bus:''' From {{ill|JR Shingu Station|ja|新宮駅}}, 1 hour via Kumano Kotsu buses. * '''Car:''' Parking available. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.hongutaisha.jp/ Official Website of Kumano Hongu Taisha] * {{short description|Shinto shrine in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|Kumano Hongū Taisha|熊野本宮大社}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shrine Kumano hongu torii01.jpg | caption = Shrine Gate (Torii) of Kumano Hongu Taisha with flag representing [[Yatagarasu]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|50|24|N|135|46|26|E|display=title,inline|source:dewiki}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現) | location = 1110 Hongucho Hongu, [[Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]] 647-1731, Japan }} {{nihongo|'''Kumano Hongū Taisha'''|熊野本宮大社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the jurisdiction of [[Tanabe, Wakayama]], deep in the rugged mountains of the southeast [[Kii Peninsula]] of [[Japan]]. It is included as part of the [[Kumano Sanzan]] in the [[World Heritage Site]] "[[Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range]]". The main deity enshrined is Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現). All of the ancient [[Kumano Kodō]] routes lead to the Grand Shrine. It was originally located at present {{Nihongo|Ōyunohara|大斎原}}, on a sandbank at the [[confluence]] of the [[Kumano River]] and Otonashi River. In 1889, it was partially destroyed in a flood and the remaining shrine buildings were relocated at its present site in 1891. Of the original five main pavilions only three were rebuilt. Four deities were moved there and the other eight are still enshrined there in two stone monuments. [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Torii at Ôyunohara.jpg|alt=Largest Torii in the world|left|thumb|Otorii]] In 2000, the largest [[torii]] shrine gate in the world (33.9 meters tall and 42 meters wide) was erected at the entrance to the Oyunohara sandbank. It is an official gateway that designates the entrance to a sacred area. It signifies the division of the secular and the spiritual worlds. This torii is called ''Otorii'' (''o'' means "great") and is made of steel weighing 172 tons, which took about six months to make and another six months to assemble.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tb-kumano.jp/en/world-heritage/kumano-hongu-taisha/|title = Kumano Hongu Taisha 熊野本宮大社|date = |accessdate = October 9, 2014|website = Sacred Kumano|publisher = Tanabe City Kumona Tourism Bureau|last = |first = }} == History == [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Shaden.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha main temple]] Over 900 years ago a pilgrim wrote of a massive shrine grounds including five main pavilions enshrining 12 deities. Numerous other small temples and shrines could be found surrounding the main buildings. Over the centuries the pavilions were partially destroyed by periodic fires and flooding, but always faithfully rebuilt to their original state. The last fire was in 1776 and the buildings rebuilt again in 1803. The first drawing of the shrine grounds from over 800 years ago and the reconstruction that took place in 1803 are almost exactly identical. After the flood of 1889, the shrine pavilions were moved and rebuilt at their present location. == Architecture == The Kumano Hongu Taisha's pavilions are an outstanding example of Japanese shrine architecture. The use of natural unfinished materials allows it to blend effortlessly into the natural environment. Intricate joint works were used in the construction instead of nails. The thick roof gracefully sweeps forward extending over the stairs and the area in front of the shrine. It is made entirely of hinoki, Japanese cypress bark. [[File:Kumano Hongu Taisha's roof architecture.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha rooftop]] The bronze ornaments on the roof top are characteristic features of shrine architecture. The X-shaped crosspieces that pierce the sky are called Chigi and the log like beams that are laid horizontally along and perpendicular to the ridge line are called Katsuogi. They add a dramatic highlight to the roof line. Unique to the Kumano Hongu Taisha is the space or corridor under the verandas of the pavilions. In the past, the pilgrims and ascetics would use this tiny refuge for meditation, prayer, [[sutra]] copying, austere rites and even sleeping quarters. In fact, this is where Saint [[Ippen|Ippen Shonin]] was enlightened. The Kumano Hongu Taisha is a mixture between Kasuga and Taisha styles but because of this sacred corridor it has also been referred to as the Kumano style. == Festivals == '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Spring Festival''', the annual spring festival held 13–15 April every year, is not only a quintessential festival of Kumano but also intimately associated with the pilgrimage to Kumano and the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. On April 13 fathers and their young sons purify themselves in the [[sacred waters]] of Yunomine Onsen before walking over the Dainichi-goe section of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route to Oyunohara wearing traditional costumes. The young boys have the character for big on their forehead and are forbidden to touch the ground. On April 15 the Kumano Deities are invoked to temporarily take up residence in a portable mikoshi shrine and return to their original site of descend, Oyunohara. The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]
Haiden (Worship Hall) | location = {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Hongu, Tanabe|ja|本宮町本宮}} 1100 | coordinates = {{Coord|33|50|24.9|N|135|46|24.9|E|display=inline,title}} | deities = {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} | shrine_rank = {{ubl|{{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}})|Former {{ill|Kanpei-taisha|ja|官幣大社}}|{{ill|Bekkaku shrine|ja|別表神社}}}} | founded = Traditionally attributed to the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign | pilgrimage = {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道}} (4th station in Wakayama) | festival = April 15 ([[Kumano Hongu Taisha Grand Festival|御田祭]]) | main_building = {{ubl|{{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (First and Second Halls)|{{ill|Kirizuma-zukuri|ja|切妻造}} (front) and {{ill|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造}} (rear) (Third and Fourth Halls)}} | map = {{location map|Japan Wakayama|lat_deg=33|lat_min=50|lat_sec=27.1|lon_deg=135|lon_min=46|lon_sec=27.4|label=Kumano Hongu Taisha|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|33|50|27.1|N|135|46|27.4|E}}}} }} '''Kumano Hongu Taisha''' ({{ill|Kumano Hongu Taisha|ja|熊野本宮大社}}, ''Kumano Hongū Taisha'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}, Japan. Alongside {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|ja|熊野速玉大社}} and {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社}}, it forms the {{ill|Kumano Sanzan|ja|熊野三山}}. The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} as its primary deity and is a key location in the UNESCO World Heritage Site, {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}. == History == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}} at Kumano Hongu Taisha]] The exact date of the shrine's foundation is unknown, but according to legend, it was established in the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign (traditionally 2nd century CE) on a sandbank in the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}}, now known as {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}}. The shrine has been associated with numerous deities and traditions over time. {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}}, often identified with {{ill|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ}}, has unclear origins. Interpretations of the deity vary, ranging from a solar god (due to the association with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, the three-legged crow), a water god (reflecting the shrine's riverside location), to a tree deity. Other theories connect the deity to {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ}}, {{ill|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛}}, or {{ill|Itsukushima|ja|五十猛神}}.{{Cite book|author=川口謙二|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|year=1999|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}} In the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, Kumano Hongu Taisha became a major pilgrimage site, attracting emperors such as {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa}}. By the 12th century, the shrine was one of Japan's most significant religious centers. === Flood and Relocation === In 1889, the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}} flooded, devastating the shrine. Only the {{ill|Kami-sha|ja|上四社}} (First to Fourth Halls) survived and were relocated to the current site. The remaining structures, including the {{ill|Naka-sha|ja|中四社}} and {{ill|Shimo-sha|ja|下四社}}, were not rebuilt. Today, two stone altars at {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}} commemorate the lost shrines. == Deities and Structure == The shrine consists of four main halls, each enshrining different deities: {| class="wikitable" |+ '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Deities and Buddhas''' ! Hall !! name !! deity !! Honji Buddha |- | First Hall || West Front Hall || {{ill|Kumano Musubi Ōkami|ja|熊野牟須美大神}}, {{ill|Kumano Gongen|lt=Koto-sakarai|ja|事解之男神}} || {{ill|Senju Kannon|ja|千手観音}} |- | Second Hall || Central Front Hall || {{ill|Hayatama-no-Mikoto|ja|速玉之男神}} || {{ill|Yakushi Nyorai|ja|薬師如来}} |- | Third Hall || Main Hall || {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} || {{ill|Amida Nyorai|ja|阿弥陀如来}} |- | Fourth Hall || East Front Hall || {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神}} || {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|lt=Jūichimen Kannon|ja|十一面観音}} |} The halls, dating to the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, are nationally designated Important Cultural Properties.{{Cite web|url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/|title=国指定文化財等データベース|publisher=文化庁}} == Cultural Significance == === Yatagarasu === {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, a three-legged crow, is a symbol of guidance and the shrine's divine messenger. It is believed to have led {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} to the Yamato region, symbolizing wisdom and divine intervention.{{Cite news|title=八咫烏について |publisher=熊野本宮大社|url=http://www.hongutaisha.jp/%E5%85%AB%E5%92%AB%E7%83%8F/|accessdate=2020-03-23}} === UNESCO World Heritage === Kumano Hongu Taisha is part of the {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004. == Access == * '''Bus:''' From {{ill|JR Shingu Station|ja|新宮駅}}, 1 hour via Kumano Kotsu buses. * '''Car:''' Parking available. == References == {{Reflist}} == External Links == * [http://www.hongutaisha.jp/ Official Website of Kumano Hongu Taisha] * {{short description|Shinto shrine in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|Kumano Hongū Taisha|熊野本宮大社}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shrine Kumano hongu torii01.jpg | caption = Shrine Gate (Torii) of Kumano Hongu Taisha with flag representing [[Yatagarasu]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|50|24|N|135|46|26|E|display=title,inline|source:dewiki}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現) | location = 1110 Hongucho Hongu, [[Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]] 647-1731, Japan }} {{nihongo|'''Kumano Hongū Taisha'''|熊野本宮大社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the jurisdiction of [[Tanabe, Wakayama]], deep in the rugged mountains of the southeast [[Kii Peninsula]] of [[Japan]]. It is included as part of the [[Kumano Sanzan]] in the [[World Heritage Site]] "[[Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range]]". The main deity enshrined is Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現). All of the ancient [[Kumano Kodō]] routes lead to the Grand Shrine. It was originally located at present {{Nihongo|Ōyunohara|大斎原}}, on a sandbank at the [[confluence]] of the [[Kumano River]] and Otonashi River. In 1889, it was partially destroyed in a flood and the remaining shrine buildings were relocated at its present site in 1891. Of the original five main pavilions only three were rebuilt. Four deities were moved there and the other eight are still enshrined there in two stone monuments. [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Torii at Ôyunohara.jpg|alt=Largest Torii in the world|left|thumb|Otorii]] In 2000, the largest [[torii]] shrine gate in the world (33.9 meters tall and 42 meters wide) was erected at the entrance to the Oyunohara sandbank. It is an official gateway that designates the entrance to a sacred area. It signifies the division of the secular and the spiritual worlds. This torii is called ''Otorii'' (''o'' means "great") and is made of steel weighing 172 tons, which took about six months to make and another six months to assemble.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tb-kumano.jp/en/world-heritage/kumano-hongu-taisha/|title = Kumano Hongu Taisha 熊野本宮大社|date = |accessdate = October 9, 2014|website = Sacred Kumano|publisher = Tanabe City Kumona Tourism Bureau|last = |first = }} == History == [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Shaden.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha main temple]] Over 900 years ago a pilgrim wrote of a massive shrine grounds including five main pavilions enshrining 12 deities. Numerous other small temples and shrines could be found surrounding the main buildings. Over the centuries the pavilions were partially destroyed by periodic fires and flooding, but always faithfully rebuilt to their original state. The last fire was in 1776 and the buildings rebuilt again in 1803. The first drawing of the shrine grounds from over 800 years ago and the reconstruction that took place in 1803 are almost exactly identical. After the flood of 1889, the shrine pavilions were moved and rebuilt at their present location. == Architecture == The Kumano Hongu Taisha's pavilions are an outstanding example of Japanese shrine architecture. The use of natural unfinished materials allows it to blend effortlessly into the natural environment. Intricate joint works were used in the construction instead of nails. The thick roof gracefully sweeps forward extending over the stairs and the area in front of the shrine. It is made entirely of hinoki, Japanese cypress bark. [[File:Kumano Hongu Taisha's roof architecture.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha rooftop]] The bronze ornaments on the roof top are characteristic features of shrine architecture. The X-shaped crosspieces that pierce the sky are called Chigi and the log like beams that are laid horizontally along and perpendicular to the ridge line are called Katsuogi. They add a dramatic highlight to the roof line. Unique to the Kumano Hongu Taisha is the space or corridor under the verandas of the pavilions. In the past, the pilgrims and ascetics would use this tiny refuge for meditation, prayer, [[sutra]] copying, austere rites and even sleeping quarters. In fact, this is where Saint [[Ippen|Ippen Shonin]] was enlightened. The Kumano Hongu Taisha is a mixture between Kasuga and Taisha styles but because of this sacred corridor it has also been referred to as the Kumano style. == Festivals == '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Spring Festival''', the annual spring festival held 13–15 April every year, is not only a quintessential festival of Kumano but also intimately associated with the pilgrimage to Kumano and the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. On April 13 fathers and their young sons purify themselves in the [[sacred waters]] of Yunomine Onsen before walking over the Dainichi-goe section of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route to Oyunohara wearing traditional costumes. The young boys have the character for big on their forehead and are forbidden to touch the ground. On April 15 the Kumano Deities are invoked to temporarily take up residence in a portable mikoshi shrine and return to their original site of descend, Oyunohara. The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]

The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} as its primary deity and is a key location in the UNESCO World Heritage Site, {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}. == History == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}} at Kumano Hongu Taisha]] The exact date of the shrine's foundation is unknown, but according to legend, it was established in the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign (traditionally 2nd century CE) on a sandbank in the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}}, now known as {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}}. The shrine has been associated with numerous deities and traditions over time. {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}}, often identified with {{ill|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ}}, has unclear origins. Interpretations of the deity vary, ranging from a solar god (due to the association with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, the three-legged crow), a water god (reflecting the shrine's riverside location), to a tree deity. Other theories connect the deity to {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ}}, {{ill|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛}}, or {{ill|Itsukushima|ja|五十猛神}}.{{Cite book|author=川口謙二|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|year=1999|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}} In the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, Kumano Hongu Taisha became a major pilgrimage site, attracting emperors such as {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa}}. By the 12th century, the shrine was one of Japan's most significant religious centers. === Flood and Relocation === In 1889, the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}} flooded, devastating the shrine. Only the {{ill|Kami-sha|ja|上四社}} (First to Fourth Halls) survived and were relocated to the current site. The remaining structures, including the {{ill|Naka-sha|ja|中四社}} and {{ill|Shimo-sha|ja|下四社}}, were not rebuilt. Today, two stone altars at {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}} commemorate the lost shrines. == Deities and Structure == The shrine consists of four main halls, each enshrining different deities: {| class="wikitable" |+ '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Deities and Buddhas''' ! Alongside {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|ja|熊野速玉大社}} and {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社}}, it forms the {{ill|Kumano Sanzan|ja|熊野三山}}. The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} as its primary deity and is a key location in the UNESCO World Heritage Site, {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}. == History == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}} at Kumano Hongu Taisha]] The exact date of the shrine's foundation is unknown, but according to legend, it was established in the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign (traditionally 2nd century CE) on a sandbank in the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}}, now known as {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}}. Interpretations of the deity vary, ranging from a solar god (due to the association with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, the three-legged crow), a water god (reflecting the shrine's riverside location), to a tree deity. Other theories connect the deity to {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ}}, {{ill|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛}}, or {{ill|Itsukushima|ja|五十猛神}}.{{Cite book|author=川口謙二|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|year=1999|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}} In the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, Kumano Hongu Taisha became a major pilgrimage site, attracting emperors such as {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa}}. The remaining structures, including the {{ill|Naka-sha|ja|中四社}} and {{ill|Shimo-sha|ja|下四社}}, were not rebuilt. Today, two stone altars at {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}} commemorate the lost shrines. == Deities and Structure == The shrine consists of four main halls, each enshrining different deities: {| class="wikitable" |+ '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Deities and Buddhas''' ! {{short description|Shinto shrine in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|Kumano Hongū Taisha|熊野本宮大社}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shrine Kumano hongu torii01.jpg | caption = Shrine Gate (Torii) of Kumano Hongu Taisha with flag representing [[Yatagarasu]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|50|24|N|135|46|26|E|display=title,inline|source:dewiki}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現) | location = 1110 Hongucho Hongu, [[Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]] 647-1731, Japan }} {{nihongo|'''Kumano Hongū Taisha'''|熊野本宮大社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the jurisdiction of [[Tanabe, Wakayama]], deep in the rugged mountains of the southeast [[Kii Peninsula]] of [[Japan]]. It is included as part of the [[Kumano Sanzan]] in the [[World Heritage Site]] "[[Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range]]". The main deity enshrined is Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現). All of the ancient [[Kumano Kodō]] routes lead to the Grand Shrine. It was originally located at present {{Nihongo|Ōyunohara|大斎原}}, on a sandbank at the [[confluence]] of the [[Kumano River]] and Otonashi River. In 1889, it was partially destroyed in a flood and the remaining shrine buildings were relocated at its present site in 1891. Of the original five main pavilions only three were rebuilt. Four deities were moved there and the other eight are still enshrined there in two stone monuments. [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Torii at Ôyunohara.jpg|alt=Largest Torii in the world|left|thumb|Otorii]] In 2000, the largest [[torii]] shrine gate in the world (33.9 meters tall and 42 meters wide) was erected at the entrance to the Oyunohara sandbank. It is an official gateway that designates the entrance to a sacred area. It signifies the division of the secular and the spiritual worlds. This torii is called ''Otorii'' (''o'' means "great") and is made of steel weighing 172 tons, which took about six months to make and another six months to assemble.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tb-kumano.jp/en/world-heritage/kumano-hongu-taisha/|title = Kumano Hongu Taisha 熊野本宮大社|date = |accessdate = October 9, 2014|website = Sacred Kumano|publisher = Tanabe City Kumona Tourism Bureau|last = |first = }} == History == [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Shaden.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha main temple]] Over 900 years ago a pilgrim wrote of a massive shrine grounds including five main pavilions enshrining 12 deities. Numerous other small temples and shrines could be found surrounding the main buildings. Over the centuries the pavilions were partially destroyed by periodic fires and flooding, but always faithfully rebuilt to their original state. The last fire was in 1776 and the buildings rebuilt again in 1803. The first drawing of the shrine grounds from over 800 years ago and the reconstruction that took place in 1803 are almost exactly identical. After the flood of 1889, the shrine pavilions were moved and rebuilt at their present location. == Architecture == The Kumano Hongu Taisha's pavilions are an outstanding example of Japanese shrine architecture. The use of natural unfinished materials allows it to blend effortlessly into the natural environment. Intricate joint works were used in the construction instead of nails. The thick roof gracefully sweeps forward extending over the stairs and the area in front of the shrine. It is made entirely of hinoki, Japanese cypress bark. [[File:Kumano Hongu Taisha's roof architecture.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha rooftop]] The bronze ornaments on the roof top are characteristic features of shrine architecture. The X-shaped crosspieces that pierce the sky are called Chigi and the log like beams that are laid horizontally along and perpendicular to the ridge line are called Katsuogi. They add a dramatic highlight to the roof line. Unique to the Kumano Hongu Taisha is the space or corridor under the verandas of the pavilions. In the past, the pilgrims and ascetics would use this tiny refuge for meditation, prayer, [[sutra]] copying, austere rites and even sleeping quarters. In fact, this is where Saint [[Ippen|Ippen Shonin]] was enlightened. The Kumano Hongu Taisha is a mixture between Kasuga and Taisha styles but because of this sacred corridor it has also been referred to as the Kumano style. == Festivals == '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Spring Festival''', the annual spring festival held 13–15 April every year, is not only a quintessential festival of Kumano but also intimately associated with the pilgrimage to Kumano and the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. On April 13 fathers and their young sons purify themselves in the [[sacred waters]] of Yunomine Onsen before walking over the Dainichi-goe section of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route to Oyunohara wearing traditional costumes. The young boys have the character for big on their forehead and are forbidden to touch the ground. On April 15 the Kumano Deities are invoked to temporarily take up residence in a portable mikoshi shrine and return to their original site of descend, Oyunohara. The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]

{{short description|Shinto shrine in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan}} {{infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|Kumano Hongū Taisha|熊野本宮大社}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = Shrine Kumano hongu torii01.jpg | caption = Shrine Gate (Torii) of Kumano Hongu Taisha with flag representing [[Yatagarasu]] | map_type = Japan | coordinates = {{coord|33|50|24|N|135|46|26|E|display=title,inline|source:dewiki}} | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現) | location = 1110 Hongucho Hongu, [[Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]] 647-1731, Japan }} {{nihongo|'''Kumano Hongū Taisha'''|熊野本宮大社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in the jurisdiction of [[Tanabe, Wakayama]], deep in the rugged mountains of the southeast [[Kii Peninsula]] of [[Japan]]. It is included as part of the [[Kumano Sanzan]] in the [[World Heritage Site]] "[[Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range]]". The main deity enshrined is Kumano [[Gongen]] (熊野権現). All of the ancient [[Kumano Kodō]] routes lead to the Grand Shrine. It was originally located at present {{Nihongo|Ōyunohara|大斎原}}, on a sandbank at the [[confluence]] of the [[Kumano River]] and Otonashi River. In 1889, it was partially destroyed in a flood and the remaining shrine buildings were relocated at its present site in 1891. Of the original five main pavilions only three were rebuilt. Four deities were moved there and the other eight are still enshrined there in two stone monuments. [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Torii at Ôyunohara.jpg|alt=Largest Torii in the world|left|thumb|Otorii]] In 2000, the largest [[torii]] shrine gate in the world (33.9 meters tall and 42 meters wide) was erected at the entrance to the Oyunohara sandbank. It is an official gateway that designates the entrance to a sacred area. It signifies the division of the secular and the spiritual worlds. This torii is called ''Otorii'' (''o'' means "great") and is made of steel weighing 172 tons, which took about six months to make and another six months to assemble.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tb-kumano.jp/en/world-heritage/kumano-hongu-taisha/|title = Kumano Hongu Taisha 熊野本宮大社|date = |accessdate = October 9, 2014|website = Sacred Kumano|publisher = Tanabe City Kumona Tourism Bureau|last = |first = }} == History == [[file:Kumano-hongû-taisha Shrine - Shaden.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha main temple]] Over 900 years ago a pilgrim wrote of a massive shrine grounds including five main pavilions enshrining 12 deities. Numerous other small temples and shrines could be found surrounding the main buildings. Over the centuries the pavilions were partially destroyed by periodic fires and flooding, but always faithfully rebuilt to their original state. The last fire was in 1776 and the buildings rebuilt again in 1803. The first drawing of the shrine grounds from over 800 years ago and the reconstruction that took place in 1803 are almost exactly identical. After the flood of 1889, the shrine pavilions were moved and rebuilt at their present location. == Architecture == The Kumano Hongu Taisha's pavilions are an outstanding example of Japanese shrine architecture. The use of natural unfinished materials allows it to blend effortlessly into the natural environment. Intricate joint works were used in the construction instead of nails. The thick roof gracefully sweeps forward extending over the stairs and the area in front of the shrine. It is made entirely of hinoki, Japanese cypress bark. [[File:Kumano Hongu Taisha's roof architecture.jpg|thumb|Hongu Taisha rooftop]] The bronze ornaments on the roof top are characteristic features of shrine architecture. The X-shaped crosspieces that pierce the sky are called Chigi and the log like beams that are laid horizontally along and perpendicular to the ridge line are called Katsuogi. They add a dramatic highlight to the roof line. Unique to the Kumano Hongu Taisha is the space or corridor under the verandas of the pavilions. In the past, the pilgrims and ascetics would use this tiny refuge for meditation, prayer, [[sutra]] copying, austere rites and even sleeping quarters. In fact, this is where Saint [[Ippen|Ippen Shonin]] was enlightened. The Kumano Hongu Taisha is a mixture between Kasuga and Taisha styles but because of this sacred corridor it has also been referred to as the Kumano style. == Festivals == '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Spring Festival''', the annual spring festival held 13–15 April every year, is not only a quintessential festival of Kumano but also intimately associated with the pilgrimage to Kumano and the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route. On April 13 fathers and their young sons purify themselves in the [[sacred waters]] of Yunomine Onsen before walking over the Dainichi-goe section of the Kumano Kodo pilgrimage route to Oyunohara wearing traditional costumes. The young boys have the character for big on their forehead and are forbidden to touch the ground. On April 15 the Kumano Deities are invoked to temporarily take up residence in a portable mikoshi shrine and return to their original site of descend, Oyunohara. The atmosphere is serene, traditional, authentic and inspiring. '''Yata-no-Hi Matsuri Fire Festival''' takes place on the last Saturday of August, in Oyunohara (Hongu-cho), in honour of [[Yatagarasu]]. This fire festival includes the parading of a fire mikoshi, a Taiko drum show, dancing, and fireworks. == Access == * Busses from: ** [[West Japan Railway Company]], [[Central Japan Railway Company]] [[Shingū Station]] on [[Kisei Main Line]] ** JR-West [[Kii-Tanabe Station]] blues ** [[Nanki–Shirahama Airport]] {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Kumano Hongu Taisha | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Inside the Kumano Hongu Taisha.jpg|270px]]

Alongside {{ill|Kumano Hayatama Taisha|ja|熊野速玉大社}} and {{ill|Kumano Nachi Taisha|ja|熊野那智大社}}, it forms the {{ill|Kumano Sanzan|ja|熊野三山}}. The shrine enshrines {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}} as its primary deity and is a key location in the UNESCO World Heritage Site, {{ill|Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range|ja|紀伊山地の霊場と参詣道}}. == History == [[File:Kumano-hongû-taisha_Shrine_-_Stone_monument_of_a_crow_"Yatagarasu".jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}} at Kumano Hongu Taisha]] The exact date of the shrine's foundation is unknown, but according to legend, it was established in the 65th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s reign (traditionally 2nd century CE) on a sandbank in the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}}, now known as {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}}. The shrine has been associated with numerous deities and traditions over time. {{ill|Ketsumi-miko Ōkami|ja|家都美御子大神}}, often identified with {{ill|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ}}, has unclear origins. Interpretations of the deity vary, ranging from a solar god (due to the association with {{ill|Yatagarasu|ja|八咫烏}}, the three-legged crow), a water god (reflecting the shrine's riverside location), to a tree deity. Other theories connect the deity to {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ}}, {{ill|Kukurihime|ja|菊理媛}}, or {{ill|Itsukushima|ja|五十猛神}}.{{Cite book|author=川口謙二|title=日本の神様読み解き事典|year=1999|publisher=柏書房|isbn=978-4-7601-1824-3}} In the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, Kumano Hongu Taisha became a major pilgrimage site, attracting emperors such as {{ill|Emperor Toba|ja|鳥羽天皇}} and {{ill|Emperor Go-Shirakawa|ja|Emperor Go-Shirakawa}}. By the 12th century, the shrine was one of Japan's most significant religious centers. === Flood and Relocation === In 1889, the {{ill|Kumano River|ja|熊野川}} flooded, devastating the shrine. Only the {{ill|Kami-sha|ja|上四社}} (First to Fourth Halls) survived and were relocated to the current site. The remaining structures, including the {{ill|Naka-sha|ja|中四社}} and {{ill|Shimo-sha|ja|下四社}}, were not rebuilt. Today, two stone altars at {{ill|Ōyunohara|ja|大斎原}} commemorate the lost shrines. == Deities and Structure == The shrine consists of four main halls, each enshrining different deities: {| class="wikitable" |+ '''Kumano Hongu Taisha Deities and Buddhas''' !
